scene.testo: In ancient Rome, your day started before the sun did. There was no coffee, no alarm clock, no snooze button. You got up in the dark, in the cold, and got dressed by feel.
Within twenty minutes, you had to be standing outside a rich man's house in the street. Why? Because if you weren't there, you didn't eat that day. That's not an exaggeration. That was the system.

For hundreds of years, this was daily life for hundreds of thousands of ordinary people. We picture togas, marble and emperors giving speeches. The reality was louder, dirtier, and stranger than any movie has ever shown you.
And here's the part that breaks most people's brains. The Romans did not have hours the way you do. So what did they do all day? And how did they know when to do it?

descrizione:
What did people in ancient Rome actually do all day? Forget togas and emperors. This cartoon history video follows an ordinary Roman from the pre-dawn knock on the door to the rich man's doorstep, where showing up decided whether you ate that day.

Discover the real daily life in ancient Rome: the crowded apartments, the loud, dirty streets, the patron and client system, and the strange way Romans measured time without hours as we know them.

Perfect for fans of Roman history, ancient history documentaries and weird history. Watch to the end and ask yourself: could you survive a single day in the Roman Empire?
